# E4 — the fast refresh: can the profile be refreshed without running the program again, and can the model's own report of the dependences close what that leaves open?

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** running

## The question

After the model has rewritten a loop, the agent profiles the whole program again; the fast refresh compiles only and carries the last run's dependences over, so the code the model just wrote has no measurement. Does that change whether the agent keeps a rewrite (H6's second half), does the model's own report of the dependences of its new lines repair it (H7), is adding dependences safe where deleting them is not (H7b) — and how many seconds does one refresh save where the run is long? In four steps, the cheap ones first (the author, 12 Oct): (1) the saved rewrites of the model replayed without a model, (2) the model's report on the rewrites that differ, (3) the time on programs with a long run, (4) live trials only if steps 1 and 2 say the refresh keeps DiscoPoP's verdicts. (RQ6, RQ7, C3)

## Result in one paragraph

Step 1 is read out (12 Oct; `e4_replay`, no model, 33 minutes on the server): 599 of the 601 pragma-free rewrites that passed the checks in the trials of E1-v6, E3 and E3b were judged after a fast refresh, after a full re-profile and after a second full re-profile as the control. The fast refresh changes whether the agent keeps the rewrite in 58 of 599, the control in 0 — the registered test E4-1: p = 0.000326, at most 0.0176 in the campaign's family of 54: H6's second half is refuted. 22 rewrites are kept only after the full re-profile — 20 of them loops the model turned into a reduction, for which the fast refresh makes DiscoPoP write `firstprivate` of the accumulator, a directive the agent's clause check refuses — and 13 of the 22 are rewrites their trial shipped; 2 are kept only after the fast refresh; 34 are kept after both with other directives, 27 of those differing only in a redundant `shared` clause (counted as the same, not registered: 31 differ, p = 0.000977, bound 0.0527). DiscoPoP's verdict on the rewritten lines differs in 417 of 599 (control 0). No time is saved on these loops: one refresh 1.54 s against 1.75 s, and with the gate's checks on the extra directives 1,758 s against 1,730 s in total. Steps 2 to 4 are open: step 2 (the model's report on the rewrites that differ) starts only after its exact cost has been put to the author.

Kept only after the fast refresh rare — 2. **Reading.** The fast refresh is not a cheaper way to the same decisions on these loops: it loses exactly the rewrites whose value lies in a dependence the model created — a reduction — because that dependence is nowhere in the profile it carries forward; and it saves nothing there, because skipping the run shortens a refresh of 1.75 s by 0.2 s and the extra directives then cost more than that at the gate. What it does not show: the speed half of the decision; what the live agent would do next after a different decision (step 4); programs whose run is long (step 3). The trials' rewrites were written by a model that had been told what the FULL profile said about its earlier attempts. **What follows:** step 2 — whether the model's own report of the dependences of its rewrite, merged into the fast refresh's profile, gives DiscoPoP the missing dependence back (H7), and what deleting does (H7b). (b) *The decision* — the unit of the registered hypotheses, 'decisions that differ from a full re-profile': whether the rewrite would be kept, speed aside — kept after both with the same directives, reverted after both, kept only after the full re-profile, kept only after the fast refresh, or kept after both with other directives. A fast refresh that reports itself unusable is counted apart: the agent then profiles in full. A new member of the campaign's family: the bound is p × 54. Refuted if the fast refresh changes the decision on more loops' rewrites than the control does; the counts are given beside the p. The time half of H6 is step 3's; the seconds of each refresh are recorded here for these programs. H7 and H7b are step 2's, on the rewrites this step finds different. **Expected, written now** — after the tool's tests on rewrites outside the population and three rewrites of one trial of the population (`e3b_1`, `s314`, repeat 1, replayed on the Mac while the tool was built, verdicts only): the fast refresh makes DiscoPoP report nearly every rewritten loop as freely parallel, because the code the rewrite created has no observed dependence — in the tests a plain `parallel for` where the full profile gives a reduction, and directives on the repetition loop and on inner loops. So (a) differs in most rewrites in which either says parallel. For (b): the gate refuses most of the extra directives, so most decisions are the same; decisions that differ are expected mainly as 'kept only after the full re-profile' — a reduction that the fast refresh turns into a plain `parallel for`, which the checks refuse — in a number I do not predict beyond 'more than a few'; 'kept only after the fast refresh' is expected rare. If (b) differs nowhere, H6's second half stands on these loops and step 2 has nothing to repair; that would surprise me and would be reported as it is. **Read-outs fixed now:** the two tables per experiment and per loop; the statuses crossed; the loops with a directive only after one of the two; the gate's verdicts on the directives of each; what becomes of the rewrites the trials themselves kept; the control beside each count; the test; the agreement with the trials' logged verdicts; the seconds. **Limits, said before the run.** The decision's speed half is not replayed; the judgement is made on one profile of each program; the live agent would continue differently after a different decision, which a replay does not show (step 4 is for that); the trials' rewrites were written by a model that had been told what the FULL profile said about its earlier attempts. **Where and how long:** the server, the DiscoPoP with B23 and B24 repaired, four 12-core groups (parts `e3_r`, `e3_d`, `e3b`, `e1v6` in the folder of `e4_replay`), after the regression of B24 is read; about 40 s a rewrite on the Mac with the gate and before the control was added, so about two to three hours.
